schemes.description: Optional graduate capstone-like course at Fisher College of Business: teams of 4-6 students, advised by a faculty functional expert, solve a business challenge for a host organisation over a 14-week spring semester, ending in a virtual presentation, analysis and recommendations to the client. Hosts include multinationals, start-ups, nonprofits and government agencies.

schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Fisher MBA (full-time second-year with 3.0 GPA and Business Lab Challenge MBA 6292; working-professional MBA with 35 graded hours); other graduate students per search summary

schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Core courses with B or better; GPA 3.0; application required (deadline 1 Oct 2026)
schemes.credit_assessment: 3 credits, graded (page calls it both 'elective' and 'required three-credit spring course')

schemes.project_evidence: Teams deliver 'a virtual presentation of project findings, an in-depth analysis, and specific, actionable recommendations to the client' [1].
schemes.group_evidence: 'teams of 4 - 6 students' advised by a faculty functional expert [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Host organisations (multinationals, start-ups, nonprofits, government agencies) supply the challenge and receive findings and recommendations as client [1]; search summary: about 50 hosts since 2013 (fisher.osu.edu GAP page).

schemes.participation_data: Approx. 50 host companies and more than 300 graduate students since 2013 (cumulative; search summary of Fisher GAP page)

profile_md: Ohio State's verified employer-linked group project provision is distributed across colleges rather than institution-wide. The strongest current route is the Industrial Design capstone, where 2025/26 teams of four or five each worked with a named sponsor (Honda, Huntington National Bank, ODNR, Neighborhood Design Center) through to a Spring 2026 exhibition. The Fisher College of Business Global Applied Projects course places MBA teams of 4-6 with multinational, start-up, nonprofit and government hosts for 14 weeks, but only an October 2026 application deadline was found, so delivery is recorded as announced. The College of Engineering's Multidisciplinary Capstone (ENGR 5901/5902) is large (over 1,000 seniors presented team capstones in April 2026) and sponsored by 50+ organisations cumulatively, but no page shows that external clients are the norm for the route, so the employer criterion is Unclear. Two further routes (Arts and Sciences industry-partner capstone, Glenn College PUBAFRS 5620 with government/nonprofit sponsors) fit the criteria in design, but only undated pages were found. The legacy STEP programme is a mentored individual-proposal programme with no evidenced team or employer project. Participation in all routes is optional or programme-specific; no compulsory university-wide scheme found. Uncertain: sponsor mix, credit and dated delivery for several routes.
gaps: Reduced-depth review (about 9 searches plus fetches). Further departmental capstones (CBE, ME, CSE, SIMCenter, Knowlton) likely; undergraduate Fisher Global Consulting not evidenced; no science-department routes found; health/law/architecture not specifically evidenced; STEP eligibility page not opened. Fisher MAP name from brief not found. Some details come from search summaries (labelled) and not page text. Page text via WebFetch was returned as summaries by the fetch tool, not raw HTML.
